ImageDescription.value:
Distorted, warped and compressed panoramic photo taken with a mobile phone in September 2026 from the top of Mount Nesaksla, the "town mountain" immediately east of Åndalsnes in Rauma Municipality, Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The image is part of a series of photographs showing the views from there. The filename indicates what the images show, including some of the following:
  • Romsdalen Cable Car (Norwegian: Romsdalsgondolen, "Romsdalen Gondola"), a two-cabin aerial gondola linking the centre of Åndalsnes with Mount Nesaksla (708 m above sea level), which opened in 2021. Its lower station is located at Jernbanekaia in the harbour on the Isfjorden, close to Åndalsnes Station and the Norwegian Mountaineering Centre. At the upper station on the summit is Restaurant Eggen, with panoramic views and outdoor seating, toilets, picnic areas, partly stone-paved and marked trails, "sherpa steps", viewing platforms and other facilities. See the Romsdalen Cable Car website.
  • Mount Nesaksla, a "town mountain" offering panoramic views. From the platform outside the upper station of the Romsdalen Cable Car (708 m above sea level), there are views of the surrounding fjord and mountain landscape:
West: the centre of Åndalsnes, the harbour and the Romsdalsfjord, which opens westwards towards Molde. The Romsdalsfjord extends approximately 70 km eastwards along the southern side of the islands of Tautra and Sekken (outside Tomrefjord and south of Otrøya), to the mouth of the Rauma at Åndalsnes and Isfjorden farther inland. In the town are, among other things, Åndalsnes Station, the Norwegian Mountaineering Centre, which opened in 2016, and MS Bolette, a 238-metre-long cruise ship owned by Fred. Olsen Cruise Lines.
North and east: Isfjorden, an arm of the Romsdalsfjord, and the village of Isfjorden, the starting point of the famous Romsdalseggen ridge and the distinctive Kirketaket mountain.
South: the most dramatic peaks, including the almost vertical Romsdalshornet, the massive Store Venjetinden and the jagged peaks of Trolltindane. Further up Isterdalen towards Trollstigen are the mountains Bispen and Kongen, and the gentler mountain ranges towards Sunnmøre.
  • Romsdalen, a valley approximately 60 km long between Åndalsnes/Veblungsnes and Lesjaskogsvatnet. The Rauma river flows through the valley. It is surrounded by high, steep mountains, including Romsdalshornet (1,550 m above sea level) and Venjetindane (1,852 m) to the east, and Trolltindane (1,797 m) to the west.
  • Romsdalshornet, a 1,550-metre mountain rising almost vertically from Romsdalen, approximately 15 km southeast of Åndalsnes.
  • Setnesfjellet, 1,238 m above sea level.
  • Adelsbreen, a glacier northwest of Store Trolltinden.
  • Store Trolltinden, approximately 1,788 m above sea level.
  • Isterdalen Valley, a side valley of Romsdalen approximately 4 km upstream from Åndalsnes, with Trolltindane on its eastern side.
  • Rauma, a 64-km-long river in Romsdalen, flowing through Lesja and Rauma Municipality. It flows northwestwards and reaches the Romsdalsfjord near Veblungsnes.
